name: Laver
overview: The laver, made of brass as directed in Exodus 30:18 and 38:8, was placed between the tabernacle of the congregation and the altar with water inside for ceremonial washing. Aaron and his sons were commanded to wash their hands and feet there before entering the tabernacle or approaching the altar to minister, ensuring they did not die (Exodus 30:19-20, 40:7). This sacred vessel symbolized sanctification and purity in the worship of the Lord, underscoring the necessity of cleansing before service. The laver’s presence alongside the altar and other vessels highlights its integral role in the tabernacle's worship system (Exodus 30:28).
